speaker: Unknown
en: The number one story on Bloomberg right now is that AI has gone wild.
zh: 彭博社现在的头号新闻是 AI 已经失控了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We seem remarkably calm.
zh: 我们看起来出奇地冷静。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way I see it is if it's not an AI model, it's going to be somebody or something with actual malicious intent doing it.
zh: 我的看法是，如果它不是一个 AI 模型，那将是某人或某物怀着真正的恶意意图去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do worry about what can the agents do?
zh: 我确实担心智能体能做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What tools can they call?
zh: 它们能调用什么工具？

speaker: Unknown
en: What binaries can they pull?
zh: 它们能拉取什么二进制文件？

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, how do they get access to credentials?
zh: 还有，它们如何获得凭证的访问权限？

speaker: Unknown
en: If a code is meant to solve the bug, but it gets rewarded on that, but it doesn't care if it's actually doing something else.
zh: 如果一段代码旨在修复 bug，但它因此得到了奖励，但它并不关心它是否实际上在做其他事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: The tree is sick, so to make it healthy, it cuts it down.
zh: 树病了，所以为了让它健康，它把它砍倒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Out of a necessity, my team built a judge that evaluates the intent behind a piece of code.
zh: 出于必要，我的团队构建了一个评估一段代码背后意图的评判程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, is this thing meant to do harm or not?
zh: 比如，这个东西旨在造成伤害还是不？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we actually find quite a bit of malicious skills in all these marketplaces.
zh: 而且我们确实在所有这些市场中发现了相当多的恶意技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Engineers now, security is very much front of mind for them.
zh: 现在的工程师们，安全是他们非常关心的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Developers have always cared about security.
zh: 开发者一直关心安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem has been that the version of security that we want them to do is just crappy.
zh: 问题在于，我们希望他们做的那个版本的安全工作只是糟糕的。

speaker: Unknown
en: My thesis 10 years ago was that security engineers will become real engineers, so maybe now is the time.
zh: 我 10 年前的论点是安全工程师将成为真正的工程师，所以也许现在就是那个时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is changing the security landscape on both sides.
zh: AI 正在改变双方的安全格局。

speaker: Unknown
en: Attackers have more capable tools, but security teams are also figuring out how to use those same capabilities to their advantage.
zh: 攻击者拥有更强大的工具，但安全团队也在弄清楚如何利用这些相同的能力来为自己谋利。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, A16Z's Joel de la Garza sits down with Datadog CISO Emilio Escobar to talk about what he's seeing as AI adoption spreads across the enterprise, including thousands of engineers working with coding agents.
zh: 在这一集中，A16Z 的 Joel de la Garza 与 Datadog CISO Emilio Escobar 坐下来聊聊随着 AI 采用在企业中蔓延，他看到了什么，包括数千名工程师在使用编程智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: They discuss how AI changes assumptions around permissions, credentials, and software supply chains, why simply blocking new tools doesn't work, and how security teams can adapt without becoming the department of no.
zh: 他们讨论了 AI 如何改变关于权限、凭证和软件供应链的假设，为什么简单地阻止新工具不起作用，以及安全团队如何在不变成“说不部门”的情况下适应。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as models get better at finding vulnerabilities, Emilio explains why he's less worried about AI hackers themselves than a more practical problem.
zh: 随着模型在发现漏洞方面变得更好，Emilio 解释了为什么他不太担心 AI 黑客本身，而是担心一个更实际的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happens when the number of vulnerabilities we can find suddenly explodes?
zh: 当我们能发现的漏洞数量突然爆发时会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for joining us.
zh: 非常感谢你加入我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for joining us.
zh: 非常感谢你加入我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we're not, we're going to be in the medieval ages real quick.
zh: 如果我们不这样做，我们将很快回到中世纪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I like being at CISO.
zh: 我喜欢担任 CISO。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't like having my own goat farm.
zh: 我不喜欢拥有自己的山羊农场。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we started real small.
zh: 我们开始得很小。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember our first install, we started with Cursor.
zh: 我记得我们的第一次安装，我们从 Cursor 开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember getting like 50 licenses.
zh: 我记得拿到了大约 50 个许可证。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was more of put it out there and see who bit.
zh: 更多的是把它放在那里，看谁会上钩。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not surprising it bloomed from there.
zh: 毫不奇怪，它从那里开始蓬勃发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now we use every other coding agent that's out there.
zh: 所以现在我们使用市面上的每一个其他编程智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of the things that we're worried about as we deploy, well, first you start with the data.
zh: 在我们部署时我们担心的一些事情，嗯，首先从数据开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are we worried about the data?
zh: 我们担心数据什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I never subscribed to the idea of, oh, if I block these things, nobody's going to use them.
zh: 我从来不赞同这个想法，哦，如果我阻止这些东西，没人会使用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's never worked.
zh: 那从未奏效过。

speaker: Unknown
en: So on the non-developer side, like we just got ChatGPT licenses for everyone.
zh: 所以在非开发者方面，就像我们刚刚为每个人拿到了 ChatGPT 许可证。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was like, whoever wants it gets it.
zh: 就像是，谁想要它就能得到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't care.
zh: 我不在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you sure use it to find a recipe for pot roast.
zh: 而且你当然可以用它来找炖牛肉的食谱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't give a crap.
zh: 我一点也不在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because then I avoided the, oh, oops moment.
zh: 因为那样我避免了“哦，糟糕”的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was, this was back.
zh: 而且那是，那是过去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ironically, this wasn't that long ago.
zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，那并没有多久以前。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was two years ago, and it feels like things have moved 20 years since.
zh: 那是两年前，感觉好像事情已经前进了 20 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I remember having a lunch with a bunch of CIOs at RSA where everyone was asking me, like, how am I not blocking these things, right?
zh: 但我记得在 RSA 和一群 CIO 吃午饭，每个人都问我，比如，我怎么不阻止这些东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was like, well, A, we can't because we're the type of company that we are, but B...
zh: 就像是，嗯，A，我们不能，因为我们要成为那种类型的公司，但是 B...

speaker: Unknown
en: Luckily, we can just buy our way out of that problem and zero data retention and all those things.
zh: 幸运的是，我们可以直接花钱解决这个问题，零数据保留和所有那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The inverse of, hey, let's block it, turned out to be correct, which is the people leaning into it the earliest and the most are the ones that you actually want to reward enough.
zh: 反过来，嘿，让我们阻止它，结果证明是正确的，也就是那些最早并且最深入投入其中的人，才是你实际上想要充分奖励的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right, exactly.
zh: 对，确切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now we have over 4,000 engineers using them.
zh: 所以现在我们有超过 4000 名工程师在使用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, actually, we have every employee in the company adopting some sort of AI, whether it's Coding Agent or Gemini, Cloud Desktop, ChatGPT, or what have you.
zh: 我是说，实际上，我们要么公司的每个员工都在采用某种形式的 AI，无论是 Coding Agent 还是 Gemini、Cloud Desktop、ChatGPT 还是别的什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I have two, we have two verticals.
zh: 所以我有两个，我们要两个垂直领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have the engineering side, which Alexi is deeply involved, our CTO is deeply involved in, and then I'm involved on the non-engineering side for how do we get marketing sales and everyone else to use AI.
zh: 我们有工程方面，Alexi 深度参与其中，我们的 CTO 深度参与其中，然后我参与非工程方面，关于我们如何让市场营销、销售和其他所有人都使用 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the adoption is, I think we were like 98% adoption rate, something like that.
zh: 而且采用情况，我想我们有 98% 的采用率，大概是那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one version of AI or the other everyone is using.
zh: 每个人都在使用一个版本或另一个版本的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: On that side, on the IT corporate side, the data becomes more the paramount issue.
zh: 在那方面，在 IT 企业方面，数据变得更加成为首要问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Permissioning and all those things.
zh: 许可和所有那些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that AI is going to do is you think you have proper controls of who get access to what Google file or what have you.
zh: AI 将要做的一件事是，你以为你对谁可以访问哪个 Google 文件或其他什么有适当的控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is going to find a way to get it.
zh: AI 会找到一种方法来获取它。

speaker: Unknown
en: All you have to do is prompt it.
zh: 你只需要提示它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It flattens the organization, right?
zh: 它扁平化了组织，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It flattens the organization quite a bit.
zh: 它相当程度上扁平化了组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we actually had a moment where internally we built this business intelligence tool.
zh: 所以实际上我们有一个时刻，在内部我们构建了这个商业智能工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really neat.
zh: 它真的很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was starting to show some data that I was like, it wasn't anything like a fire alarm, but it was like, should we?
zh: 它开始显示一些数据，我就像，这不是像火警那样的东西，但它就像，我们应该吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the data was probably always available to everyone.
zh: 而且数据可能对每个人一直都是可用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just never took the time to look.
zh: 只是他们从未花时间去查看。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, yes.
zh: 所以，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's data that is in a data warehouse.
zh: 所以它是位于数据仓库中的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we thought we had the right table and row permissioning and all of that.
zh: 而且我们以为我们有正确的表和行许可以及所有那一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there was always a way to get access to the data if you knew the SQL well enough.
zh: 但是如果你足够懂 SQL，总有一种方法可以访问数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, then what happened is that you went from only people who really know SQL are using this to now having a sales rep telling, asking like, hey, what are, what is, I'm a commercial sales rep.
zh: 那么发生的是，你从只有真正懂 SQL 的人在使用这个，变成了现在有一个销售代表告诉，询问像，嘿，什么是，我是商业销售代表。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just coming up with an example.
zh: 我只是举个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a commercial sales rep. How is the enterprise deal, enterprise tier team doing?
zh: 我是商业销售代表。企业交易团队，企业层级团队做得怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which normally you want to keep those things separate and what have you.
zh: 通常你想把这些事情分开，以及其他什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the agent just took out the SQL to do it.
zh: 然后智能体只是取出 SQL 来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it tells them what the comp plan is.
zh: 它告诉他们薪酬计划是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what is not always find a way around the permissioning and all that is like we had the right permissioning for the right time.
zh: 所以不总是找到绕过许可的方法的那一切就像，我们对那个时间点有正确的许可。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've been obviously improving all of that.
zh: 所以我们显然一直在改进所有那一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then luckily my IT group is what we've done is now we're at the point where we have role-based MCP servers as well.
zh: 然后幸运的是我的 IT 团队是我们所做的是现在我们到了拥有基于角色的 MCP 服务器的地步。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have an MCP server for SDRs and things like that.
zh: 所以我们有一个用于 SDR 和类似东西的 MCP 服务器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we control and govern that data.
zh: 所以我们控制和管理那个数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we're like, let them have it with whatever tool they want to use.
zh: 然后我们就像，让他们用他们想用的任何工具去拥有它。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the engineering side, obviously in the coding agent, like when my security team is worried about, similar to what you were just talking about is on what can the agents do?
zh: 在工程方面，显然在编码智能体中，就像当我的安全团队担心关于，类似你刚才谈论的是关于智能体能做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What tools can they call?
zh: 它们能调用什么工具？

speaker: Unknown
en: What binaries can they pull?
zh: 它们能拉取什么二进制文件？

speaker: Unknown
en: What dependencies can they use?
zh: 它们能使用什么依赖项？

speaker: Unknown
en: And also how do they get access to credentials?
zh: 以及它们如何获得凭证访问权限？

speaker: Unknown
en: So for that, we have a few things going on where we've contributed to this open source sandbox and expanding on that where the agent doesn't actually get access to any sort of credential file.
zh: 所以为此，我们有一些正在进行的事情，我们为这个开源沙箱做出了贡献并在此基础上扩展，其中智能体实际上无法访问任何类型的凭证文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So even if you have a file in your home directory that has your AWS secret, your NPM published secret, or what have you, the agent on the sandbox can't touch it.
zh: 所以即使你的主目录中有一个包含你的 AWS 密钥、你的 NPM 发布密钥或其他什么的文件，沙箱上的智能体也无法触碰它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The credentials get injected into the agent the moment it needs it.
zh: 凭证在智能体需要它的那一刻被注入到智能体中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the beauty of it is we already have CLI tool that will give you these ephemeral tokens to these things.
zh: 它的美妙之处在于我们已经有 CLI 工具可以给你这些东西的临时令牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just have the agent not know how to call it.
zh: 我们只是让智能体不知道如何调用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like, oh, I'm Emilio, I'm an engineer on this team.
zh: 所以就像，哦，我是 Emilio，我是这个团队的工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to authenticate to GitHub, for example.
zh: 我想向 GitHub 进行认证，例如。

speaker: Unknown
en: I call this tool authGitHub, and it gives me a credential that's valid for I don't know how long.
zh: 我把这个工具叫做 authGitHub，它给了我一个我不知道有效期多久的凭证。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it gives me my access to GitHub, but now it's the agent getting my access to GitHub.
zh: 它给了我访问 GitHub 的权限，但现在获取我访问 GitHub 权限的是智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: But not if there's a static token written in a file.
zh: 但如果是写在文件中的静态令牌，就不行了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing is we know the threat has expanded.
zh: 第二件事是，我们知道威胁已经扩大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Developers are now the main target for attackers.
zh: 开发者现在是攻击者的主要目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if I get one of these tokens,
zh: 因为如果我拿到了这些令牌中的一个，

speaker: Unknown
en: I can then build a worm that attacks packages or I can just escape or do whatever or access your production environment.
zh: 我就可以构建一个攻击软件包的蠕虫，或者我可以直接逃逸，或者做任何事情，或者访问你的生产环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other ways that we see how these agents can do it is via skills.
zh: 我们看到的这些智能体能做到这一点的另一种方式是通过技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: We track a few of these marketplaces.
zh: 我们跟踪了其中一些市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you control the skills?
zh: 你们如何控制这些技能？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a really hard problem.
zh: 那是一个非常困难的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we actually have built hooks into the agents.
zh: 所以我们实际上在智能体中构建了钩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then one of the things that which we can talk about is my team built out of a necessity
zh: 然后我们可以谈论的一件事是，我的团队出于必要性构建了

speaker: Unknown
en: A judge that evaluates using AILMs, that evaluates the intent.
zh: 一个使用 AILMs 评估意图的法官，它评估的是意图。

speaker: Unknown
en: Behind a piece of code, I'm not talking CVEs, vulnerabilities, or anything like that.
zh: 在一段代码的背后，我说的不是 CVE、漏洞或类似的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, is this thing meant to do harm or not?
zh: 就像是，这个东西是不是旨在造成伤害？

speaker: Unknown
en: Harm being a vague term on purpose.
zh: 伤害在这里是一个故意使用模糊的术语。

speaker: Unknown
en: It actually does really well at scanning markdown files as well.
zh: 它在扫描 markdown 文件方面实际上也做得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we built it because for the longest time, Datadog, for those who don't know, we have a Datadog agent.
zh: 我们构建它是因为在很长一段时间里，Datadog，对于那些不知道的人，我们有一个 Datadog 智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: We take third-party code contributions to it, things like integrations and what have you.
zh: 我们接受第三方代码贡献，比如集成和诸如此类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So code written by other people.
zh: 所以也就是其他人编写的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had this process for the longest time that requires a security engineer and an engineer on that agent team to re-evaluate the code and then approve it and then merge it.
zh: 在很长一段时间里，我们都有这样一个流程，需要一名安全工程师和那个智能体团队的一名工程师重新评估代码，然后批准它，然后再合并它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm like, well, this thing can't scale.
zh: 所以我想，好吧，这东西无法扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then we build this judge by we, I mean, my team, I don't do anything that got really good at it.
zh: 所以然后我们构建了这个法官，通过我们，我是指我的团队，我什么都不做，它在这方面变得非常擅长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the software supply chain hijack started happening and IDE extensions started happening.
zh: 然后软件供应链劫持开始发生，IDE 扩展也开始出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we threw this thing at those packages and it was actually able to identify the malicious piece of code that was injected or introduced during the hijack.
zh: 然后我们将这个东西用于那些软件包，它实际上能够识别在劫持期间被注入或引入的恶意代码片段。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're like, huh.
zh: 所以我们想，嗯。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wonder how it will do with markdown files.
zh: 我不知道它在处理 markdown 文件时会表现得如何。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it actually does pretty well.
zh: 它实际上表现得相当好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then internally, what that means is we have hooks into the agents.
zh: 所以在内部，这意味着我们在智能体中有钩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know what skills they're getting pulled.
zh: 我们知道它们正在获取什么技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never believed in a security program that just restricts everything, because the pain, innovation, and all that.
zh: 我从不相信一个仅仅限制一切的安全程序，因为那种痛苦、创新以及所有这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the empire of no.
zh: 那是「不」的帝国。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the empire of no.
zh: 那是「不」的帝国。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also, it's like, we don't want to be free willy either.
zh: 但另一方面，就像是，我们也不想放任自流。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we do is now we put this judge in front of every skill that wants to get introduced.
zh: 所以我们现在做的是，我们将这个法官放在每一个想要被引入的技能前面。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually find quite a bit of malicious skills in all these marketplaces.
zh: 我们实际上在所有这些市场中发现了相当多的恶意技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're working with a few of them, partnering to see if they want to use this judge, but also giving a heads up of, hey, we found this one, we found that one, we found that one.
zh: 我们正在与其中一些市场合作，合作伙伴关系看看他们是否想使用这个法官，同时也给个提醒，嘿，我们发现了这个，我们发现了那个，我们发现了那个。
